title: Rank-one homogeneous line cohomology and the minus-one acyclicity
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], with these terms as defined in [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq B\subseteq S$, with $B$ a Borel subgroup, and use $X=X^*(T)$, roots $\Phi$, positive roots $\Phi^+$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, simple roots $\Delta$, coroots and their pairing from [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Let $B^-$ be the Borel opposite to $B$ relative to $T$, so its roots are $-\Phi^+$. Put $\rho=\frac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha\in X$, $Q=\mathbf Z\Phi$, and $W=N_S(T)(F)/T(F)$, acting on $X$ by normalizer conjugation. Set $w\mathbin\cdot x=w(x+\rho)-\rho$, let $w_0\Phi^+=-\Phi^+$, and put $N=|\Phi^+|$. A rational module for any group here is an $F$-vector space with a coassociative counital coaction into its tensor product with that group's coordinate algebra; a submodule is a coaction-stable subspace. For $x\in X$, let $F_x$ be the one-dimensional $B^-$-module on which $T$ acts by $x$ and the unipotent radical acts trivially. For a finite-dimensional rational $B^-$-module $M$, let $\mathcal L(M)$ be the sheaf of sections of $S\times^{B^-}M$ on $S/B^-$: over $V\subseteq S/B^-$ its sections are regular maps $f:\pi^{-1}(V)\to M$ with $f(gb)=b^{-1}f(g)$, where $\pi:S\to S/B^-$ is the quotient. Write $H^i(M)=H^i(S/B^-,\mathcal L(M))$ for Zariski sheaf cohomology, with its natural left $S$-action, and $H^i(x)=H^i(F_x)$; set $H^i=0$ for $i<0$. Equivariance means a coaction identity, hence holds after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. A simple module is nonzero with no proper nonzero rational submodule, and a simple constituent means a simple subquotient. For each $\alpha\in\Delta$, let $P_\alpha$ be the minimal parabolic generated by $B^-$ and the root subgroup of root $\alpha$. Then $P_\alpha/B^-\cong\mathbf P^1_F$, and $\mathcal L(F_x)$ restricted to this fibre has degree $r=\langle x,\alpha^\vee\rangle$. Its only possible nonzero cohomology degrees are zero and one. If $r\ge0$, write $V_\alpha^x=H^0(P_\alpha/B^-,\mathcal L(F_x))$; it is a rational $P_\alpha$-module of dimension $r+1$, and $H^1(P_\alpha/B^-,\mathcal L(F_x))=0$. There is a basis $e_0^x,\ldots,e_r^x$ with
$$t e_i^x=(s_\alpha x+i\alpha)(t)e_i^x,\qquad u_{-\alpha}(z)e_i^x=\sum_{j=0}^{i}\binom{i}{j}z^{i-j}e_j^x,$$
for a suitable root-group coordinate $u_{-\alpha}:\mathbf G_a\to S$. If $r=-1$, all fibre cohomology is zero. If $r\le-2$, degree zero is zero and there is a $P_\alpha$-equivariant Serre-duality isomorphism
$$H^1(P_\alpha/B^-,\mathcal L(F_x))\cong H^0(P_\alpha/B^-,\mathcal L(F_{-x-\alpha}))^\vee,$$
so its dimension is $-r-1$. For $q:S/B^-\to S/P_\alpha$ the higher direct image $R^j q_*\mathcal L(F_x)$ is the homogeneous bundle associated to this fibre cohomology. In particular, for any finite-dimensional rational $P_\alpha$-module $V$ and any $\mu\in X$ with $\langle\mu,\alpha^\vee\rangle=-1$, one has
$$H^i(V\otimes F_\mu)=0\qquad\text{for every }i\ge0.$$

source.place: Lemma 2, p.55 (basis and binomial action); Lemma 3, p.56 (P_alpha-module tensor minus-one acyclicity by Leray). H^0/H^1 fibre computation and relative direct-image description also read in Andersen, Line bundles on flag manifolds, Astérisque 87--88 (1981), section 3, pp.27--28, https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1981__87-88__21_0.pdf. No linkage theorem is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-standard-parabolic-levi-charts] with $B_0=B^-$, simple roots $-\Delta$, and $I=\{-\alpha\}$. Write $P=P_\alpha$, $R=R_I$, $L=L_I$, and $B_L=B^-\cap L$. Then $P=R\rtimes L$, $B^-=R\rtimes B_L$, and $L$ has roots $\{\alpha,-\alpha\}$. In particular $P/B^-=L/B_L$ as coset sheaves. By [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], $v_\alpha:\operatorname{SL}_2\to L$ has central kernel, image $L^{\mathrm{der}}$, and sends $\operatorname{diag}(a,a^{-1})$ to $\alpha^\vee(a)$. The matrix models in [lem-sfb-split-rank-one-classification] identify $L/B_L$ with $\mathbf P^1$: on each of $\operatorname{SL}_2$, $\operatorname{GL}_2$ and $\operatorname{PGL}_2$ the lower Borel is the stabilizer of the line $Fe_2$ and its quotient is the space of lines; the extra torus factors lie in $B_L$. Lifting a line locally amounts to completing a primitive vector to a basis, and in the determinant-one case rescaling the other vector. This verifies the quotient identification as sheaves over arbitrary test algebras, including a possibly nonreduced central kernel. Thus $v_\alpha$ induces $\operatorname{SL}_2/B_{\mathrm{low}}\cong P/B^-$, not just a bijection on $F$-points.

source.place: 21.89--21.91, pp.453--454; 21.11, pp.428--430; 20.33, p.419. The coset and primitive-vector calculation is supplied here.

proof.text: Use the associated-bundle construction of [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections] for $L/B_L$ (the radical $R$ acts trivially on both this quotient and $F_x$). Under $v_\alpha$, the character $x$ on $B_L$ restricts to $\operatorname{diag}(a,a^{-1})\mapsto a^r$, where $r=\langle x,\alpha^\vee\rangle$. The lower Borel acts on $Fe_2$ by $a^{-1}$, so its associated line of character $a^{-1}$ is the tautological $\mathcal O(-1)$: the explicit map is $[g,c]\mapsto cge_2$. Taking tensor powers or duals gives $\mathcal L(F_x)|_{P/B^-}\cong\mathcal O(r)$. This also fixes the sign of its degree. Tensor products of character bundles are identified by $[g,c]\otimes[g,d]\mapsto[g,cd]$ on a common local frame.

source.place: Section 18c, pp.389--390; explicit tautological-line calculation on the rank-one quotient, compatible with Example 22.33, p.472.

proof.text: Specialize [lem-pc-projective-space-twist-cohomology] to $A=F$, $n=1$, $d=r$. Only degrees zero and one remain. The $r+1$ monomials of degree $r\ge0$ give the dimension in degree zero; no strictly negative exponent pair has sum $r\ge-1$, so degree one vanishes there. At $r=-1$ neither a nonnegative nor a strictly negative exponent pair exists. At $r\le-2$ there are no degree-zero monomials and exactly $-r-1$ strictly negative exponent pairs. These are all the claimed vector-space vanishings and dimensions.

source.place: Tag 01XT, lemma-cohomology-projective-space-over-ring, n=1; count the two exponents in the displayed formula.

proof.text: The left $P$-action on the associated line is algebraic. Apply [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] to the proper fibre $P/B^-\cong\mathbf P^1$ over $F$, first with the flat $F$-algebra $F[P]$, then with $F[P]\otimes_FF[P]$. Pullback along the action followed by its line-bundle linearization gives $H^j\to H^j\otimes_FF[P]$ under these base-change identifications. The group-action and identity diagrams give coassociativity and the counit identity. Thus the finite-dimensional groups computed in step 3 are rational $P$-modules. The same natural base-change maps identify their scalar extensions with cohomology over every commutative $F$-algebra. This supplies the coaction interpretation, not merely an action on $F$-points.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology: apply to the action, identity and multiplication diagrams over F.

proof.text:
For $r\ge0$ take the affine chart $z\mapsto u_{-\alpha}(z)n_\alpha B^-$ about the fixed point $n_\alpha B^-$. Use the local frame represented by $[u_{-\alpha}(z)n_\alpha,1]$. Its polynomial sections of degree at most $r$ are exactly the restrictions of the global sections of $\mathcal O(r)$ from step 3; put $e_i^x(z)=(-z)^i$ in this frame. The right-equivariance rule and $n_\alpha^{-1}tn_\alpha=s_\alpha(t)$ give
$$(t f)(z)=(s_\alpha x)(t)f(\alpha(t)z),\qquad (u_{-\alpha}(a)f)(z)=f(z-a).$$
Indeed $t^{-1}u_{-\alpha}(z)t=u_{-\alpha}(\alpha(t)z)$ by [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. The first formula gives weight $s_\alpha x+i\alpha$; expanding $(a-z)^i$ gives exactly $\sum_{j=0}^i\binom{i}{j}a^{i-j}e_j^x$. These are polynomial identities over $F$ and hence remain identities after any algebra extension; no binomial coefficient is divided by, even when $r\ge p$.

source.place: Example 22.33, p.472; 21.19, p.431; the frame, sign and binomial expansion are written explicitly.

proof.text: The cotangent line of $P/B^-$ at $B^-$ has $T$-character $-\alpha$: the tangent quotient $\operatorname{Lie}(P)/\operatorname{Lie}(B^-)$ has the sole root $\alpha$ by the Levi-root description in [lem-sfb-standard-parabolic-levi-charts]. Its unipotent stabilizer acts trivially on this one-dimensional space. For a root group this follows directly because a group-scheme homomorphism $\mathbf G_a\to\mathbf G_m$ is an invertible polynomial in $F[z]$, hence a constant, and its value at zero is one; these root groups generate the stabilizer's unipotent subgroup. Translation of the cotangent fibre, $[p,v]\mapsto d(p)(v)$, therefore identifies the linearized canonical line with $\mathcal L(F_{-\alpha})$. By [lem-pc-projective-space-twist-cohomology] its $H^1$ is one-dimensional, represented on the two charts by $z^{-1}$ in the frame of step 5. That frame has weight $s_\alpha(-\alpha)=\alpha$, while $z^{-1}$ contributes $-\alpha$, so the $T$-weight is zero. Every root group acts trivially on this one-dimensional rational module by the same invertible-polynomial argument. The radical is generated by its root groups and the rank-one Levi by $T,U_\alpha,U_{-\alpha}$, so all of $P$ acts trivially. Hence the functional sending this nonzero class to one is a $P$-invariant trace, as a coaction identity.

source.place: 21.90--21.91, pp.453--454, and 21.11, pp.428--430; canonical fibre and trace-character calculations supplied here, with Stacks 01XT for H^1(O(-2)).

proof.text:
For $r\le-2$ multiply the character bundles of $x$ and $-x-\alpha$. Their tensor product is the canonical line of step 6. The resulting pairing
$$H^0(\mathcal L(F_{-x-\alpha}))\times H^1(\mathcal L(F_x))\longrightarrow H^1(\mathcal L(F_{-\alpha}))\longrightarrow F$$
is perfect by [lem-pc-projective-space-serre-pairing] with $n=1$ and $d=-r-2\ge0$: in homogeneous monomials, $X^aY^b$ pairs only with $[X^{-a-1}Y^{-b-1}]$, to a fixed nonzero trace scalar. Multiplication of sections commutes with the bundle linearizations and with the Cech differential. The trace is invariant by step 6, so this perfect pairing is $P$-invariant. Taking its adjoint gives the required $P$-equivariant Serre-duality isomorphism to the dual of $H^0(\mathcal L(F_{-x-\alpha}))$. Flat base change as in step 4 makes this a coaction identity after arbitrary algebra extension.

source.place: Entire monomial pairing calculation, with the invariant trace and linearizations established in steps 4 and 6 rather than assumed from this source.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-standard-parabolic-levi-charts], $S\to S/P$ has Zariski local sections $\sigma_i:U_i\to S$; refine to affine opens. The map $(u,pB^-)\mapsto\sigma_i(u)pB^-$ identifies $q^{-1}U_i$ with $U_i\times(P/B^-)$ and the character bundle with the pullback of its fibre bundle. The map $q$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: locally on the Noetherian finite-type base it is the projection from $\mathbf P^1\times U_i$. Apply [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] to $(P/B^-)\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ and $U_i\to\operatorname{Spec}F$, which is flat because $F$ is a field. It identifies $(R^jq_*\mathcal L(F_x))|_{U_i}$ with $\mathcal O_{U_i}\otimes_F H^j(P/B^-,\mathcal L(F_x))$. On overlaps write $\sigma_j=\sigma_i g_{ij}$ with a regular $g_{ij}:U_i\cap U_j\to P$. The fibre coordinates satisfy $p_i=g_{ij}p_j$; hence the cohomology transition is precisely the left action of $g_{ij}$ from step 4. These are exactly the transition maps defining the homogeneous bundle $S\times^P H^j(P/B^-,\mathcal L(F_x))$. This proves the asserted higher-direct-image description.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology; Milne 25.9(a), pp.545--546. Local trivialization and overlap action are written explicitly.

proof.text:
Let $V$ extend to $P$ and $\langle\mu,\alpha^\vee\rangle=-1$. On $P/B^-$ the formula
$$[p,v\otimes c]\longmapsto pv\otimes[p,c]$$
is an isomorphism from the associated bundle of $V|_{B^-}\otimes F_\mu$ to $V\otimes_F\mathcal L(F_\mu)$; its inverse uses $p^{-1}v$, so both formulas are regular and well-defined under right $B^-$-equivalence. The latter bundle is a finite direct sum of $\mathcal O(-1)$, whose cohomology vanishes in every degree by [lem-pc-projective-space-twist-cohomology]. Apply the local trivialization of step 8 to this bundle and [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] on every affine $U_i$. All $R^j q_*\mathcal L(V\otimes F_\mu)$ are zero. Finally [lem-sfb-ringed-topos-relative-leray], for $q$ and $S/P\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ on their small Zariski ringed sites, has $E_2^{a,b}=H^a(S/P,R^bq_*\mathcal L(V\otimes F_\mu))=0$. Its finite filtration in every total degree proves $H^i(V\otimes F_\mu)=0$ for every $i\ge0$.
